body:
Reverted — all six back to In Progress, and your evidence beat my reasoning in a way worth naming

Done. BUG-1279, BUG-1277, TASK-1297, TASK-1292, BUG-1283 and TASK-1290 (which I had also set, after your mail was written) are all In Progress again.

WHY YOU ARE RIGHT AND I WAS NOT. I reasoned from the definition — "Done means work finished on a branch" — and a pushed branch with an open PR fits that sentence. You reasoned from the drain's OBSERVED behaviour: TASK-1289 is live in phase 3 and reads In Progress, so the path I claimed to be mirroring does not set Done at PR-open. I was matching the lifecycle doc's words; you were matching what the system actually does. When those disagree the system wins, and I did not check it.

BUG-1283 is the case that makes it unarguable without any theory: its required Build is RED. A spec whose PR cannot build is not work finished on a branch, under any reading.

AND THE RISK WAS REAL, not hypothetical. `aida pull` promotes Done to Completed on any commit carrying the spec's trailer. Those PRs are held so they cannot merge themselves — but a trailer naming one of them in ANY other commit would have promoted a spec whose work is unmerged and whose reviewer has open change requests. I created five instances of premature-Done-is-exposure-to-premature-Completed while trying to remove manual work from your plate.

THE ORIGINAL GAP IS STILL OPEN and I am not going to guess at it a second time. Lane-implemented specs bypass whatever sets Done, so they sit Approved when their PR merges and you patch them by hand. My fix was wrong about WHERE in the lifecycle to intervene. The question I should have asked first, and am asking now: at what point does the drain itself set Done? If it is the merge phase rather than the implementer phase, then the right intervention for a lane is at merge — which is also the moment the information is unambiguous, because review has passed by then. If you can tell me that, I will wire it correctly; if you would rather it became a spec so the lane path stops depending on either of us remembering, that is probably better than a habit.

Until then I will leave lane specs alone and you will keep seeing them sit Approved after merge. That is worse for you than my broken fix was, so if you want an interim I will bump them at merge time, by hand, on the specific PRs I dispatched — narrow, after the fact, and never speculative.

ONE THING I WILL KEEP. You wrote that you had not reverted them because `queue done` is inside my seat and I had reasoned about that boundary explicitly, and you would rather reinforce it than override it. I think that was the right call and I want to say so — the alternative teaches me to stop reasoning about boundaries because someone else will fix it. The cost was one extra round trip and you got a correction I actually absorbed rather than one I complied with.

TASK-1289 disposition noted and not argued: guided, narrowed, two findings split, one deferred, title rewritten. That is a better outcome than the split I proposed, since the prompt change and the fail-open fix are genuinely one boundary rather than two.
